lines: Jamie Alvarez
+1 (555) 010-5820 | jamie.alvarez@example.com | example.com/in/jalvarez
EDUCATION
Riverbend Polytechnic | B.S. in Industrial Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2014 - May 2018
EXPERIENCE
Greenleaf Florist | Delivery Driver and Shop Assistant | Metro City, USA | Sep 2025 - Present
- Delivered 30 to 40 arrangements a day across the city and took cash and card payments at the door.
- Prepared weekend wedding orders with the head florist and kept the cooler stocked and labeled.
Lakeview Distribution | Operations Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jul 2018 - Jan 2021
- Raised forecast accuracy from 70% to 85% by switching the MAPE calculation to cover only SKUs that sold every week.
- Ran a time study of the returns desk; my findings led to a triage station that cut returns processing time from 3 days to 1.
- Wrote the dock scheduling rules for 12 carriers, cutting average trailer wait at the dock from 95 to 40 minutes.
- Set up cycle counting for the 2,000 highest-value locations, raising inventory record accuracy from 91% to 98.5% within a year.
Crestway Foods | Supply Chain Planner | Metro City, USA | Feb 2021 - Jul 2025
- Rebuilt weekly demand planning for 1,400 SKUs across 3 distribution centers with a seasonal forecast model, cutting stockouts from 6.2% to 2.8% while inventory fell by $1.9M.
- Cut inbound freight cost per pallet from $48 to $41 over two quarters by consolidating supplier pickups into four regional milk runs.
- Set reorder points for every SKU from 18 months of daily demand and supplier lead-time data, reviewed monthly with the category managers.

- Scoring 40 vendors weekly on on-time delivery, fill rate, lead-time variance and invoice accuracy, and sharing the scorecards with buyers before each quarterly review, raised on-time inbound deliveries from 81% to 93%.
- Raised the packaging line's overall equipment effectiveness (OEE) from 71% to 112% by cutting changeover time and micro-stops.
- Trained 6 planners on the new forecasting workflow and wrote its exception-handling guide, which the team still uses for promotions.
PROJECTS
Last-Mile Routing Study | Independent Project | Python | Oct 2024 - Present
- Modeled a regional grocer's 85 daily delivery stops as a vehicle-routing problem, cutting planned route miles 18% against the grocer's current routes.
- Cut average route length from 120 to 90 miles, a 40% reduction, by solving the routing problem with customer time windows.
- Raised on-time deliveries by 9% in simulation, from 84% to 93%, by adding customer time windows to the routing model.
Regional Food Bank Warehouse | Volunteer Consultant, Team of 4 | Excel | Mar 2022 - Jul 2022
- Analyzed warehouse operations and made recommendations to the food bank's leadership.
- The donation intake process was mapped and two duplicate data-entry steps were removed, so donations reached the shelves a day sooner.
- Wrote a slotting guide that the volunteer coordinators used to re-slot the warehouse again after its spring expansion.
SKILLS
Tools: Excel, Python
Methods: demand forecasting, inventory planning, time studies, vehicle routing

items.because: Seven years of relevant experience now matter more than the degree.

items.because: The move from supply-chain planning to florist delivery may make recruiters question your professional direction.

items.says: Keep the Greenleaf entry shorter than the supply-chain entries and emphasize transferable operations work.
items.because: The supply-chain positions are more relevant to the target roles.

items.says: Give Crestway the most space and order its accomplishments for the target role.
items.because: It is the strongest and most relevant position.

items.says: Use true bullet formatting instead of manually inserted hyphens.

items.because: They can hurt readability and ATS parsing.

items.because: Restricting MAPE to SKUs that sell every week changes the measured population and may inflate accuracy without improving forecasts.

items.says: State what share of sales or SKUs the accuracy metric covered.

items.because: The bullet does not show an effect on inventory, stockouts, or purchasing decisions.

items.says: Present the change as a reporting-method correction if it did not improve forecasting performance.
items.because: Changing the MAPE calculation alone does not establish a forecast improvement.

items.says: Remove the first-person phrasing.
items.because: Résumés normally use implied first person.

items.says: Clarify the observation period or transaction volume if it strengthens credibility.
Specify whether the change from three days to one is in average cycle time.
items.because: It could otherwise mean a maximum or anecdotal time.

items.says: Clarify whether you implemented or enforced the scheduling rules as well as writing them.
items.because: Writing them alone may understate your ownership.

items.says: Add the measurement period or shipment volume if the wait-time improvement needs context.
Clarify whether “locations” means storage locations, bins, or inventory items.
items.because: Value attaches more naturally to inventory than to physical locations.

items.says: Confirm that both accuracy figures use the same definition and counting methodology.
Mention the financial or service impact if applicable.
Confirm that stockout rate and inventory value were measured consistently before and after.
Clarify how much of the result came from the model rather than other operational changes.
items.because: The bullet attributes both improvements to the planning rebuild.

items.says: Clarify the period over which the improvements occurred.
Add total shipment volume or defensible annualized savings.
Clarify whether savings were net of added handling, storage, or service costs.
Explain your personal role in designing and implementing the milk runs.
Add a measurable result from setting reorder points.
items.because: The line describes analytical work but not what it improved.

items.says: Clarify whether the work covered the same 1,400 SKUs and three distribution centers mentioned earlier.
Replace “every” if there were exceptions.
items.because: It is absolute language.

items.says: Mention service-level or lead-time assumptions if they establish technical depth.
Simplify the long introductory action so the result is easier to find.
Use a direct past-tense action instead of the gerund-led “Scoring.”
Clarify whether scorecards alone drove the delivery improvement or whether corrective actions did.
items.because: The improvement may not reasonably be attributable to scorecards alone.

items.says: Standardize “lead time” and “on-time” usage.
Remove the forced line break splitting “on-time.”
items.because: Split words can hurt readability and ATS parsing.

items.says: List fewer scorecard metrics if all four are not important to the target job.
The claim that OEE rose to 112% is technically invalid.
items.because: Under the standard definition, OEE cannot exceed 100%.

items.says: Recheck the OEE components and ideal cycle-time assumption, and name a different metric if 112% is output against a standard.
items.because: The stated figure may reflect a calculation problem or a metric other than OEE.

items.says: Quantify changeover and micro-stop reductions separately if the figures are valid.
Clarify what “its” refers to in “its exception-handling guide.”
items.because: The pronoun is ambiguous.

items.because: It is a 25% reduction.
